judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer does not flag the Dimauro22 citation or challenge its scope qualifiers. No mention of 'Dimauro22' or the over-generalisation of the sample to all galaxies at all redshifts appears anywhere in the report.
The review discusses morphology catalogs and dust/systematics but does not challenge the Dimauro22 citation or claim that the cited result was overgeneralized beyond massive galaxies at 0<z<2.
While the reviewer discusses morphological classification and Section 4.3, they do not mention Dimauro22 or challenge the specific claim about its sample composition.

The reviewer does not flag the Dimauro et al. (2022) citation in Section 4.3, nor does the reviewer challenge the scope of that claim (missing 'massive' and 'at 0<z<2' qualifiers). The reviewer's comments on morphology focus on classification biases and catalog merging, not on the over-generalization of the Dimauro22 result.

The reviewer's summary accurately quotes '~290,000 galaxies' (matching the abstract), but never flags the contradiction with a '~29k' figure in the Summary/conclusion section. The inconsistency between the two sections is not noted.
The reviewer consistently summarizes the sample as ~290,000 galaxies and does not flag any contradiction between the abstract and summary/conclusion sample-size figures, nor mention a ~29k value.
The reviewer cites the correct figure (290,000) from the abstract in their summary but does not detect the contradictory smaller value in the paper's summary section.

The reviewer discusses the parameterisation in Section 3.1 (Major Comment 3) but only questions whether gamma_2 should be fixed to zero at z>2, not the spurious 1/2 prefactor inserted in front of the log term in Eq. (1).
Although the reviewer comments on the modeling choice of fixing gamma_2=0 at z>2, they do not identify any algebraic error in Eq. (1) or mention an incorrect 1/2 prefactor on the logarithmic term.
The reviewer critiques the logic of fixing parameters in the functional form described in Section 3.1, but does not identify the erroneous 1/2 factor in Equation 1 itself.
The reviewer does not flag any cross-reference mismatch between Figure 8 and Figure 9, nor any inconsistency between the prose description of the star-forming subsample and the figure it references.
The review contains no flag about an incorrect figure cross-reference in Section 4.3 and does not mention Figure 8 versus Figure 9 for the star-forming subsample analysis.
The reviewer mentions several figures but does not flag the cross-reference error between Figure 8 and Figure 9.
